source_fields.instance: The unknown matrix $A\in\mathbb C^{d\times d}$ is Hermitian positive definite, satisfies $\kappa(A)=\kappa>1$, and has at least $t+1$ distinct eigenvalues. The vector $b\ne0,\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and function $h$ are public; either $h$ or $h(z)/z$ belongs to the specified Stieltjes class.

assumptions.description: The spectrum is positive, $\operatorname{cond}(A)=\kappa$, with at least $t+1$ distinct eigenvalues.

The function $h$ or $h(z)/z$ admits the representation $\int_0^\infty(z+s)^{-1}\,d
u(s)$, with positive $
u$ and $\int(1+s)^{-1}\,d
u(s)<\infty$.

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: Assume integers $t\ge1$ and $d\ge t+1$, actual condition number $\kappa>1$, and arbitrary real $\alpha$. The vector $b$ may cause early Krylov termination.

operations.query_signature: Input any vector v in C^d
operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact complex vector responses, without observation noise or rounding

operations.coupling: One fixed Hermitian matrix; queries are determined by the exact Lanczos recurrence starting from b
operations.index_control: The algorithm selects vectors and an available channel; block width is charged by column.

source_fields.query_domain_description: Right products map C^d to C^d, with only the stated channel available. A q-column block costs q queries. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not additional free feedback.

source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: The output must be the fixed Lanczos-FA value. A different algorithm or Krylov approximation cannot be substituted.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.

source_fields.normalization: Use the source ratio conventions $0/0=1$ and $1/0=+\infty$. The quantity is an approximation factor, not exact-zero query complexity.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.

components.description: One right product Av with a single vector

source_fields.budget_semantics: For fixed t, Lanczos uses at most t matrix actions and possibly fewer under early termination. The native comparison target is an error factor.
source_fields.scalarization: Compare the approximation factor C of fixed Lanczos while retaining N_right. This is not minimum query complexity for an ε target.
source_fields.setup_cost: Reading public parameters and explicitly public $b,x_0,h$, mask, or tree incurs no matrix-vector call. Information about hidden $A$ comes only from native responses.
source_fields.precision_model: The interface provides exact complex Hermitian matrix–vector products. Bit costs of real or complex arithmetic are outside this factor objective.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Randomization is forbidden; the algorithm is fixed to Lanczos-FA.
source_fields.adaptivity: Determined by the same exact Lanczos recurrence
source_fields.internal_computation: Use exact single-start Lanczos with initial basis vector b/‖b‖₂. Evaluate the known small matrix function h(T_t) and return ‖b‖₂ V_t h(T_t)e₁. If an invariant subspace is reached early, return the exact result.
source_fields.parallelism: Strict single-start sequential Lanczos recurrence. Per-column charging of block calls does not authorize changing the fixed algorithm.

source_fields.complete_expression: The deterministic instancewise criterion compares fixed-Lanczos error with the smallest error in the same Krylov space $K_t$. For each admissible $A$, the lower bound selects suitable $h,b$; it is not a lower bound for every $h,b$.
source_fields.quantifier_order: fixed algorithm Lanczos-FA; sup over A,h,b

metric.normalization: Use the source ratio conventions $0/0=1$ and $1/0=+\infty$. The quantity is an approximation factor, not exact-zero query complexity.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: Define $\|z\|_{A^\alpha}=(z^*A^\alpha z)^{1/2}$ and $\mathcal K_t(A,b)=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,\ldots,A^{t-1}b\}$. The approximation factor is $\mathcal C=\|h(A)b-y_t\|_{A^\alpha}/\min_{y\in\mathcal K_t(A,b)}\|h(A)b-y\|_{A^\alpha}$, with conventions $0/0=1$ and positive numbers divided by zero equal $+\infty$.
description_paragraphs:
Define the weighted norm $\|z\|_{A^\alpha}=(z^*A^\alpha z)^{1/2}$ and Krylov space $\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,\ldots,A^{t-1}b\}$. Compare the fixed Lanczos output with the best approximation in that space through the error ratio $$
\mathcal{C}=\frac{\|h(A)b-y_t\|_{A^\alpha}}{\min_{y\in\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)}\|h(A)b-y\|_{A^\alpha}}.
$$. Use the conventions $0/0=1$ and positive numbers divided by zero equal $+\infty$.
